newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil eyes January sale of Cemig stake.
newsitem.headline: Brazil eyes January sale of Cemig stake.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) hopes to sell 33 percent of state-run Cemig power firm voting common shares in January but analysts said an auction is unlikely until later in 1997.
"The BNDES is studying how best to sell the shares," a bank spokeswoman told Reuters.
"It is foreseen for January but no date has been set yet. Nothing's been decided," she added.

Analysts, meanwhile, said federal officials are likely to push ahead with the sale but it is unlikely to take place for several months as a shareholders agreement must be rewritten and bid specifications published first.
"This transaction is therefore not likely to move forward until the later part of the first half of 1997," Bear Stearns & Co said in a report.
Brazil's Minas Gerais state had hoped to sell the shares by mid-January but scrapped its plans after the BNDES decided not to extend the deadline for repayment of a 430 million-real state debt.
BNDES granted the loan in early 1996 and was issued debentures convertible to the 33-percent stake in Cemig common shares. The first repayment tranche was due October 31.
As a result of the decision not to grant an extension, the shares now belong to the BNDES, which manages Brazil's federal privatization program.
The planned sale of the Cemig stake drew the interest of foreign firms looking to secure a toe-hold in Brazil's mammoth energy market. The state had hoped to garner $1 billion from the sale.
Under an agreement, proceeds from the sale will now be split between the firm, state and BNDES.
Minas Gerais state had held 84 percent of Cemig ordinary, or voting common shares and state lawmakers earlier this year approved the sale of a 33 percent stake to a strategic partner.
Several foreign firms expressed interest including Chile's Enersis, Southern Electric, Enron Corp , Ontario Hydro and Hydro Quebec of Canada, EDF of France and EDP of Portugal.
